=== ssh-proxy-cli 
exit 0
--- stdout
SSH SOCKS5 and HTTP proxy.

Usage:
  ssh-proxy-cli [command]

Commands:
  start [--foreground] [--wait=SECONDS]
      Start the proxy in the background
  restart [--foreground] [--wait=SECONDS]
      Restart with the current configuration
  stop
      Stop the proxy and its SSH tunnel
  status [--proxy_http] [--proxy_socks]
      Show status as JSON or print a proxy URL
  login [ENDPOINT] [--check] [--log=FILE]
      Set up passwordless SSH login
  logs [--follow] [--lines=N]
      Show or follow proxy logs
  test [--url=URL]
      Test HTTP and SOCKS5 forwarding
  check
      Validate configuration as JSON

Autostart commands (current user):
  Use "ssh-proxy-cli autostart --help" for login startup details.

  autostart enable
      Start the proxy at future logins
  autostart disable
      Remove login startup; leave the proxy running
  autostart status
      Show login registration and outdated entries

Flags:
  -h, --help      help for ssh-proxy-cli
  -v, --version   version for ssh-proxy-cli

Use "ssh-proxy-cli [command] --help" for command details.
--- stderr
=== ssh-proxy-cli start --help
exit 0
--- stdout
Start the proxy in the background

Background mode requires SSH keys or ssh-agent; run login for setup. After
--wait expires, the proxy may keep retrying; check status for readiness. --wait
has no effect with --foreground.

Usage:
  ssh-proxy-cli start [flags]

Flags:
      --foreground     Run in this terminal; Ctrl+C stops the proxy
  -h, --help           help for start
      --wait SECONDS   Wait up to SECONDS (1..3600) for background
                       readiness (default 20)
--- stderr
=== ssh-proxy-cli restart -h
exit 0
--- stdout
Restart with the current configuration

Background mode requires SSH keys or ssh-agent; run login for setup. After
--wait expires, the proxy may keep retrying; check status for readiness. --wait
has no effect with --foreground.

Usage:
  ssh-proxy-cli restart [flags]

Flags:
      --foreground     Run in this terminal; Ctrl+C stops the proxy
  -h, --help           help for restart
      --wait SECONDS   Wait up to SECONDS (1..3600) for background
                       readiness (default 20)
--- stderr

=== ssh-proxy-cli status --help
exit 0
--- stdout
Show endpoint and health as JSON. URL flags print only the selected proxy URL
when running, otherwise nothing. An empty result exits successfully.

Usage:
  ssh-proxy-cli status [flags]

Flags:
  -h, --help          help for status
      --proxy_http    Print only the running HTTP proxy URL (http://)
      --proxy_socks   Print only the running SOCKS5 proxy URL (socks5h://)
--- stderr
=== ssh-proxy-cli login --help
exit 0
--- stdout
Set up unattended SSH login, skipping steps that are already done. Without
ENDPOINT, try SSH aliases in file order until one succeeds.

If no key exists, login creates one (OpenSSH's default ~/.ssh/id_ed25519, so no
IdentityFile line is needed). It then logs in once, where you verify the host
fingerprint and may enter your server password, and adds your public key to the
server. Finally it checks that login works without prompts. Working logins exit
0 at once. If the server refuses password login, send the printed public key to
your administrator. --check only checks and changes nothing.

Usage:
  ssh-proxy-cli login [ENDPOINT] [flags]

Flags:
      --check      Check unattended login only: no prompts or new host
                   keys; the tray runs it before each start
  -h, --help       help for login
      --log FILE   Append SSH diagnostics to FILE (used by the tray)
--- stderr
=== ssh-proxy-cli logs --help
exit 0
--- stdout
Show or follow proxy logs

Usage:
  ssh-proxy-cli logs [flags]

Flags:
  -f, --follow    Follow new log lines
  -h, --help      help for logs
      --lines N   Show the last N (1..10000) lines (default 60)
--- stderr

=== ssh-proxy-cli autostart
exit 0
--- stdout
Start the proxy at login for the current user, independently of the tray app.
Enable and disable change future login startup; neither starts nor stops the
current proxy. Use start, stop or restart for that. No elevation or sudo needed.
Unattended SSH login is required. Enable warns if its login check fails, but
still registers so you can enable while offline. Windows briefly opens a console
at login. Status reports registration; changes made in OS startup settings may
not be reflected. Disable before moving the installation folder.

Usage:
  ssh-proxy-cli autostart [flags]
  ssh-proxy-cli autostart [command]

Available Commands:
  enable
      Start the proxy at future logins
  disable
      Remove login startup; leave the proxy running
  status
      Show login registration and outdated entries

Flags:
  -h, --help   help for autostart

Use "ssh-proxy-cli autostart [command] --help" for command details.
--- stderr
=== ssh-proxy-cli autostart status --help
exit 0
--- stdout
Show login registration and outdated entries

Usage:
  ssh-proxy-cli autostart status [flags]

Flags:
  -h, --help   help for status
--- stderr

--- stderr
